objective: Make event-journal reads support bounded time-range queries.
rationale: The daily operator summary scans the whole journal, which grows without bound.
architectural_intent: Keep the journal append-only and add a range predicate rather than a second index structure.

assumptions.statement: The journal exposes a monotonic sequence usable as a range key.
No caller depends on the current unbounded read returning every event.

implementation_strategy: Extend EventQuery with an inclusive upper bound and translate it to a SQL predicate. Leave existing callers unchanged by treating zero as unbounded.
interfaces: type EventQuery struct { ProjectID string; AfterSeq, UpToSeq int64 }
pseudocode: if q.UpToSeq > 0 { clauses = append(clauses, "seq <= ?"); args = append(args, q.UpToSeq) }
edge_cases: UpToSeq below AfterSeq must return an empty result, not an error.
failure_modes: A caller that forgets the bound silently reads the whole journal.

guidance.statement: The journal remains append-only; no read path may mutate events.
Zero means unbounded so that existing callers are unaffected.
Choose the clause construction style that matches the surrounding code.

acceptance_criteria: A bounded read returns exactly the events within the range.
An unbounded read behaves as before.
escalation_conditions: Assumption A2 turns out to be false.
The change would require altering the event envelope.
observability_requirements: Range reads log the bound as a correlation field.
rollback: Revert the query change; no durable data is affected.
